그래도 훅훅 읽다보면 재밌습니다 키워드가 취향이라 그런지.

Kiss the Scumbag is a modern omegaverse romance that leans fully into emotional cruelty, unresolved misunderstandings, and volatile love. The story revolves around Winston Campbell, an extreme alpha and heir to a powerful family, and Seol Yujin, an omega he once loved and now openly despises. Five years ago, their relationship ended in disaster when Winston became convinced that Yujin had betrayed him by having an affair with his father. That single misunderstanding turns love into bitterness, and Winston never lets Yujin forget it.

When a fire leaves Yujin homeless and struggling to survive with his young daughter, fate cruelly pushes him back into the Campbell estate. Winston’s father has left Yujin a large inheritance, but with a brutal condition, he must marry Winston and have a child within a year. Trapped by reality and driven by equal parts desperation and resentment, Yujin accepts. What follows is a marriage soaked in humiliation, power imbalance, and emotional retaliation. Winston insists that their relationship is nothing more than a legal obligation, yet his possessiveness and desire betray him at every turn.

Winston is very much a love-to-hate character, arrogant, cruel, and obsessive, wielding his power without restraint while refusing to confront his own feelings. Yujin, on the other hand, is quietly resilient. Outwardly soft and compliant, he carries emotional strength shaped by hardship, motherhood, and years of silent endurance. Their dynamic is messy and painful, built on hatred, attraction, and a truth neither of them is ready to face.

The tone of the story is heavy and emotionally charged. Themes of revenge, regret, possessiveness, class disparity, and parental responsibility run through the narrative. Romance here is not gentle or comforting, it is sharp, suffocating, and fueled by denial and desire. The presence of Yujin’s child adds an extra layer of tension, constantly challenging Winston’s beliefs and forcing the reader to anticipate the moment when the truth finally surfaces.

This is a story for readers who enjoy dark omegaverse romances with strong power dynamics, love-hate relationships, and morally flawed characters. It does not shy away from discomfort or emotional damage. Kiss the Scumbag is painful, dramatic, and unapologetically intense, a romance where love survives not because it is healthy, but because it refuses to die.
